messages:
sam: noticed a p99 spike (~+38ms) on host preparse at 09:20 UTC after the kernel-selector rollout. quick flame shows Tokenizer::align_copy and many grpc small writev calls.

infra-bot: perf-alert host-preparse.p99 +38ms window=10m affected=host-runtime-34*

rita: did selector pick a new vectorized kernel for short sequences? that can add align memcpy overhead.

sam: yes, selector picked vec-opt-short for seq<=48. local microbench shows p99 jumps for short seqs (seq=32 p99 44ms vs baseline 12ms).

kai: batching estimator still uses old cost table. it now underestimates vec-opt-short cost => reduces batching targets => more batches => more writev syscalls.

ops: feature-flag available: runtime.kernel.force_scalar_shortseq. can flip on canary without restart.

sam: flipping on canary now and enabling a short coalescer for grpc (ingress.coalesce_writev_ms=0.15) as mitigation. also adding per-request kernel_id tag for 12h.

ops: flags applied at 09:45 UTC (runtime.kernel.force_scalar_shortseq=true, ingress.coalesce_writev_ms=0.15).

rita: short action list: (1) kai rebench vec-opt-short vs scalar across seqs [8,16,32,48,64] and batch sizes; (2) kai update cost table and rollout script; (3) sam add kernel telemetry and KV-prefetch probe to look for miss amplification.

sam: assigned owners. monitoring canary and will post results here.

infra-bot: created ticket PERF-4360: kernel-cost-mismatch -> batching amplification.

sam: will follow up with a short postmortem once we have bench numbers. :thumbsup:
